newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest seen wet through Friday, then cooler.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest seen wet through Friday, then cooler.

text.p: Rains were expected to push eastward across the U.S. Midwest Thursday and Friday, followed by cooler temperatures, meteorologists said.
"We will be seeing cooler weather moving in after this front," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "It's not the knockout freeze people were looking for."
Clouds and rain had reached Illinois Thursday morning and were expected to hit Indiana and Ohio Thursday evening and Friday, Burgio said.
Coverage was expected to be wide across the region with rainfall amounts of 0.50 to 2.00 inches likely, he said.
Light showers were forecast for the eastern corn belt Saturday with clearer skies to the west, said Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis in his daily report.
"Next week there is no indication of any significant rain systems moving across the belt," Davis said.
Burgio forecast low temperatures in the 40s degrees Farenheit Saturday morning to the northwest. He said cloud cover and wind would limit the likelihood of a frost.
A second cold front was expected to move through Sunday and Monday, bringing some 30s F to the western corn belt, Burgio said.
Next week was expected to be mostly dry with a few scattered showers possible Wednesday, Davis said.
"The only chance of rain will be about Wednesday as a fast moving cold front sweeps from northwest to southeast across the belt," he said.
Long-range forecasts indicated temperatures could warm up late next week.
"The computers are suggesting some sort of a warm-up into next week but I'm not convinced that's going to happen," Burgio said.

The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook released Wednesday indicated normal to above normal temperatures and normal to below normal precipitation in the U.S. Midwest from October 1 through October 5.
